hero.headline: Multiple Specialities. One Familiar Clinic.
hero.subheadline: J.S.Poly Clinic brings a general physician, a paediatrician, and a gynaecologist together at one address on Mangadu Road, so most of what your family needs doesn't require crossing town.

about.title: The first call for most of what your family needs
body: J.S.Poly Clinic sits on Mangadu Road in Thirumudivakkam as a genuine polyclinic — 'poly' meaning many, because that's the whole idea. Instead of a single specialist working alone, we've put a general physician, a paediatrician, and a gynaecologist under one roof, with a shared front desk and shared records.

That matters more than it sounds. A fever that needs a general physician one week and a child's vaccination the next don't need two different clinics, two different intake forms, and two different drives across Thirumudivakkam. For most households, this one address covers most of the calendar year.
We keep the clinic open into the evening on purpose, because appointments that only exist during office hours aren't much use to people who work office hours.
highlights: General medicine, paediatrics & women's health, one address
Open evenings until 8:30 PM, Monday to Saturday
Vaccinations and minor procedures done on-site

blogPosts.title: Why a Polyclinic Can Save You a Lot of Unnecessary Referrals
blogPosts.excerpt: A single-doctor clinic often means a referral slip and a second trip across the city. Here's how having multiple specialities under one roof changes that.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Senthil Kumar
content: It's a familiar pattern in growing neighbourhoods like Thirumudivakkam: you visit a general physician for a routine issue, and it turns out the real concern falls slightly outside their scope, so you're handed a referral slip and sent across town for another consultation, another intake form, another wait.

A polyclinic — 'poly' simply meaning many — solves a good chunk of this by keeping multiple general specialities at one address. When a general physician, a paediatrician, and a gynaecologist all work out of the same clinic, a lot of what used to require a referral just becomes a conversation between doctors down the same corridor.

There's a continuity benefit too, one that's easy to underestimate until you've lived without it. When one clinic holds your family's records across specialities, a doctor treating your child can quickly reference a relevant family history, and vice versa — something far harder when care is scattered across unconnected clinics with no shared file.

None of this replaces a tertiary hospital for genuinely complex or emergency cases — a polyclinic isn't trying to be one. But for the large share of everyday health needs a family actually has in a given year, one familiar address covers most of it, and that's the whole point of the model.
